_comment: Known Microsoft-endpoint strings in the build output, each with the reason it
is not a live beacon. check-endpoints.mjs fails on anything NOT listed here,
so an upgrade that reintroduces a real endpoint is caught.
Reasons written against 1.131.0; the file list still matches exactly at
1.137.0, with no new unexplained hits. Re-verify on upgrade rather than
extending blindly: the point of the list is that adding to it requires a

allow.reason: Dead fallback in environmentService.ts:239: `productService.webviewContentExternalBaseUrlTemplate || 'https://{{uuid}}.vscode-cdn.net/...'`. staticify.mjs sets options.webviewEndpoint, which wins at line 237, so the fallback is unreachable. Confirmed by runtime network capture.

Absolute sourceMappingURL comments emitted by the minified VS Code web package. Browsers only fetch a source map when developer tools request it; RuntimeCode neither executes nor otherwise contacts vscode-cdn.net through these comments. The deployed static build does not ship a sourcemaps directory.

product.defaultChatAgent entitlement URLs, plus path fragments appended to a user-configured GitHub Enterprise host. defaultChatAgent cannot be removed (onboardingVariationA.ts:80 asserts it at module scope), so these stay as inert config. Nothing reads them because extensions/copilot is not bundled, and the entitlement flow only runs from that extension.

Same defaultChatAgent entitlement/MCP-registry URLs. Inert without the Copilot extension. They would become live if Copilot were ever installed, which Open VSX cannot currently do: it carries neither GitHub.copilot nor GitHub.copilot-chat. Left configured rather than blanked so that choice stays open.
Documentation link inside a localized UI string (the Dev Containers pointer). Rendered as text, never fetched.
Documentation links in UI strings and in TypeScript compiler diagnostic text (`Learn more at https://aka.ms/tsconfig`). Displayed, never requested.

The 1DS collector URL is a module-level constant in platform/telemetry/common/1dsAppender.ts, but the appender is only constructed at telemetryService.ts:112, which requires productService.aiConfig?.ariaKey. The OSS product.json has no aiConfig, since that key lives in the private distro mixin, so no appender is ever created and the constant is dead. Confirmed by runtime network capture.
Same 1DS SDK, bundled into Microsoft-authored built-in extensions. Gated on vscode.env.isTelemetryEnabled, which is false by default here. See the dc.services entry.

The TAS experimentation endpoint, reached through tas-client inside github-authentication. It only runs once that extension activates, which requires the user to start a GitHub sign-in, and it respects the telemetry setting. This is the least inert entry in this file: if you want it gone, drop github-authentication from the web bundle (it is opt-in and nothing else depends on it).

The ApplicationInsights SDK bundled into Microsoft-authored built-in extensions via @vscode/extension-telemetry. This is real telemetry code rather than a doc string, but it gates on vscode.env.isTelemetryEnabled, which is false because configurationDefaults sets telemetry.telemetryLevel to 'off'. Left present rather than stripped so the user retains the choice, per the settings-based approach. Drop these extensions from the bundle if you want the code gone entirely.
